features.name: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of the original post's initial premise before introducing its divergence from the OP?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Read title and argument only to identify the OP's initial premise. Return 1 if at least one single comment, in its own words, explicitly acknowledges that the OP's initial premise (the starting claim/assumption in title/argument) is valid, correct, reasonable or fair, and then, later in that same comment, introduces a point of divergence or disagreement. Acknowledgment and divergence must both occur within the same comment, in that order. Do not count generic politeness, acknowledging only a side point, or acknowledging something other than the OP's initial premise. Ignore quoted text unless the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies or the list is validly empty; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

h0: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging has no association with view change.
h1: any_comment_acknowledges_op_premise_before_diverging is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
note: Operational assumptions: 'discussions where counter-arguments...' is operationalized as at least one comment doing so (any). The OP's initial premise is judged from current title/argument, which may contain edits or outcome announcements; the extractor is told to ignore those. Comment order and timing are unknown. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.
